# Usage ledger rollout

Prisma remains pinned to 7.10.0. Campaign and worker integrations must deploy
as one runtime release. Schema migrations can deploy first. Neither migration
nor backfill enables paid gating.

## Verify on disposable PostgreSQL 16

```sh
npm run db:generate
npm run test:usage:db
npm test -- --fileParallelism=false
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
```

The runner creates a unique Docker Compose project with a random loopback port,
a random password, a `_test` database and tmpfs storage. It never connects to the
inherited development database. It runs the usage suites and the complete database
suite, then removes only that project's resources. Do not run database suites
against development data. Do not reset or drop production accounting tables.

## Cutover and backfill

1. Apply reviewed additive schema with `npm run db:deploy`. Generate the pinned
   Prisma client. Keep `paidGatingEnabled=false`.
2. Pause sending with `SystemControl.sendingEnabled=false` and stop old worker
   processes. Drain active Gmail requests before recording cutover; leases last
   two minutes, but a missing lease on an old worker requires an explicit drain.
   Do not convert attempting or uncertain work to READY. Install both runtime
   integrations while sending is paused.
3. Preview without committing any changes:

   ```sh
   npm run usage:backfill -- --dry-run
   ```

4. Apply only while sending remains paused and old workers are drained:

   ```sh
   npm run usage:backfill -- --apply
   ```

   The script records one `SystemControl.usageCutoverAt`. Every owner commits
   evidence, reservations, counters, validation, `usageCutoverAt`, and backfill
   version together. Failed owners roll back without a checkpoint; later owners
   continue. Resume with the same command. Completed owners are revalidated on
   rerun. Existing READY expiry is the original cutover plus 24 elapsed hours;
   neither reruns nor redispatch extend it. New queues expire after 24 hours.

5. Repeat the apply command to validate resumability. Require zero failed owners
   and no missing accounting before any activation. Restart the new workers and
   restore `sendingEnabled` when the cutover succeeds. A failed cutover remains
   paused until repaired.
6. Paid gating is a separate explicit operational change. The implementation,
   migrations, dry run, and apply command never flip that flag. Verify both flag
   states before activating it. Gated owners without validated accounting fail
   closed; genuinely empty new owners can initialize under their owner lock.

## Accounting and expected differences

Daily periods are UTC midnight to midnight. Free and complimentary Paid access
use UTC calendar months; actual paid subscriptions retain the exact provider
subscription ID and start/end timestamps. Grace extends that same allowance's
operational end; it does not grant a second allowance. An unresolved active
provider boundary pauses sending. A verified downgrade uses the Free calendar
month and includes paid attempts that occurred within that month. Unused capacity
does not roll over. No template, CSV, role, or reminder gating is added here.

Charges follow claim time, including an in-flight request crossing midnight.
Retained historical success uses `attemptedAt`, falling back to `sentAt` with
provenance recorded. Old receipts cannot recover a missing attempt time: their
`sentAt` fallback may approximate attribution near midnight. An unresolved legacy
attempt without an attempt timestamp is conservatively attributed to its creation
time and remains uncertain. Only known exact historical provider boundaries are
assigned directly; durable evidence seeds every subsequently created overlapping
allowance. Each charge is counted once per period, as a direct ledger reservation
or an imported baseline. Send deletion sets the ledger link to null; receipts keep
the stable delivery key and import evidence survives all history deletion.

The backfill independently reconstructs counters with SQL and validates retained
Send/Receipt identities. It also reports the unchanged legacy rolling-24-hour query.
Rolling totals and calendar totals are intentionally different: a previous UTC day's
success can remain in the rolling total, today's queued send may retain its original
reservation when deferring, and an uncertain attempt older than 24 hours stops counting
in legacy usage while still occupying its historical ledger allowance. Do not require
rolling and calendar totals to match or use their difference to issue refunds.

## Reconciliation and operational signals

The signed Inngest endpoint registers `quota-reconciliation` hourly
(`0 * * * *`, UTC), using one `reconcile-owners` step.
It pages owner IDs, settles durable acceptance, expires abandoned leases into
uncertainty, releases proven unsent terminal/expired work once, reconstructs counters,
and repairs publication after commit. A failed owner does not block others.
Publication repairs increment the dispatch generation/event ID, preserving both
the Send and delivery key. Deferrals use `availableAt`; quota waits do not create
long-running sleep loops. Definite rejections release reservations and finish
without another sending attempt. Legacy queued retries are finalized without
resubmission; their old counters remain only as evidence.

Campaign submission still dispatches immediately. Interrupted publication,
deferred sends, and accounting recovery can wait up to one hour after becoming
eligible; normal pacing still applies before the first sending attempt.
Already-sent and uncertain deliveries are never automatically resent.

`maintenance` runs daily at 03:00 UTC / 08:30 IST (`0 3 * * *`). Its single
discovery step paginates accounts internally and returns only IDs needing cleanup:
active accounts with unused attachments awaiting physical deletion. Account
deletion is owned by the separate daily deletion sweep. Current attachments and those
needed by queued, attempting, or uncertain sends remain protected. A prior
`deletedAt` marker does not exclude unfinished storage deletion. Events are sent
in batches of 100; an idle discovery emits none. The existing per-account worker
rechecks eligibility under its existing locks. Attachment backlogs beyond its
ten-file limit continue on later daily passes. Cleanup may wait up to one day
after becoming eligible, and provider failures can extend that delay.

With no pending work, the registered schedules now use at least 56 execution
units/day or 1,680 per 30 days. This includes the daily deletion-job sweep
(three steps), hourly quota reconciliation (at least one owner page),
daily attachment maintenance, and daily rate-limit
cleanup. Operator monitoring and alert delivery have been removed. Inngest counts
both function runs and steps ([execution limits](https://www.inngest.com/docs/durable-execution/limits)).
Sending, pacing, extra pages, account cleanup and retries add usage. Measure a
controlled campaign before estimating customer capacity.

After deployment, synchronize the current endpoint registrations. Verify
`account-deletion-jobs` uses `0 2 * * *` UTC,
`rate-limit-cleanup` uses `0 4 * * *` UTC, `quota-reconciliation` uses
`0 * * * *`, and `maintenance` uses `0 3 * * *`. Confirm
`minimum-hardening-monitor`, `operator-alert-delivery`, `scheduled-replies`, and
`refresh-replies`, and `deletion-maintenance` are absent. Deployment and production synchronization are
separate rollout steps.

Warnings contain only operational codes and owner/send UUIDs. Monitor
`UNCERTAINTY_OLDER_THAN_15_MINUTES`, `PUBLICATION_DELAY`, `COUNTER_DRIFT`,
`OUTSTANDING_ORPHAN`, `MISSING_ACCOUNTING`, `REPAIR_FAILED`, `PUBLICATION_FAILED`,
and `SETTLEMENT_FAILED`. Orphans are alerts, never automatic refunds. Gmail and the
database cannot guarantee atomic exactly-once acceptance. Ambiguous network failures
or lost acceptance persistence retain capacity and prevent automatic resend.
No Sent search or delivery-resolution controls are introduced. Mark replied and
Undo affect reply state only.

## Rollback

Disable paid gating to restore rolling-200 enforcement while retaining ledger
writes, claim leases, duplicate protection, and reconciliation. If accounting itself
fails, pause sending, drain workers, and repair forward. Preserve all added tables,
source identities, and uncertain attempts. Never refund an ambiguity or put it back
into READY. Do not run destructive down migrations.
